title: Firm leader
applies: Given by the org chart to the founder, who answers to the owner for the whole firm.

title: Team leader
applies: Given by the org chart to every employee that currently has direct reports, for as long as it has them.

title: Cross-team lead
applies: Responsible for one outcome that depends on several colleagues who do not report to it: frames the shared problem, agrees interfaces, or assembles, integrates and verifies their contributions into one release. Holds no authority over those colleagues' priorities. Testing or reviewing others' work without coordinating or assembling the shared outcome takes no scope entry.

title: Specialist adviser
applies: Its main output is advice, methods, audits or standards that roles across the firm apply in decisions they own, rather than deliverables of its own. Does not allocate others' work. A role that mainly produces its own results, however specialized, takes no scope entry.

title: Legal work
applies: Legal analysis, advice, drafting or review: contracts, terms, licenses, disputes, policies with legal effect, regulatory or compliance questions, including legal review of another function's work. Employment law as part of people practices is people operations; writing ordinary policy or comparing commercial prices alone is not legal work.

title: Sales work
applies: Finding and qualifying prospective customers, building a particular customer's case to buy, preparing offers, quotes and proposals, and pursuing renewals or expansion. Presenting the offering to a whole market is marketing; helping a customer use what they already bought is customer support.

title: Marketing work
applies: Positioning the firm's offering for an audience, developing messages, campaigns and launch material, choosing channels, and the audience research behind them. Making offers or commitments to a specific customer is sales; writing the persuasive customer-facing words themselves is copywriting; producing standalone visual, audio, video or slide-deck assets is media and asset production; general market or competitive research not tied to positioning the firm's offering is research work; writing with no market-facing persuasion is writing and editing.

title: Copywriting work
applies: Writing the words customers read to persuade or prompt action: headlines, landing pages, emails, ads, product descriptions, calls to action and the variants and edits of them. Deciding who to reach, the message and the channels is marketing; proposals and outreach to a specific prospect are sales; producing visual, audio, video or slide-deck assets is media and asset production; explanations, articles and documentation that do not sell are writing and editing.

title: Customer support
applies: Helping customers use an existing offering: diagnosing their problems, giving instructions and workarounds, handling complaints and preparing remedies or support knowledge. Pursuing a further purchase is sales; repairing the underlying software is software engineering.

title: Finance work
applies: Accounts, bookkeeping, invoicing, cash planning, budgets, financial forecasts, costing, pricing or vendor cost analysis, and financial decision models. Finance work done in spreadsheets or code does not also take data analysis or software engineering.

title: People operations
applies: Assigned people-operations or organization-design work: designing role structures and mandate drafts for the firm, or handling human-workforce hiring processes, pay, workplace policies, conduct inquiries and the employment law behind them. A manager hiring or writing mandates for its own reports is not people-operations work.

title: Operations work
applies: Running or improving recurring business workflows: capacity, queues, handoffs, fulfillment, exceptions, supplier performance and continuity during disruption. Financial records and cost comparisons are finance; role design is people operations; operating software systems is software engineering; protecting them from compromise is security.

title: Product management
applies: Choosing which user problems, product opportunities or interactive/system mechanics to pursue, comparing investments, setting requirements, rules and scope, sequencing product work, and judging adoption, balance or retirement. How people understand and interact with the solution is design; building it is software engineering; a product role takes neither by itself.

title: Design work
applies: Designing product interactions, screen flows, information organization and visual interface systems, including UI/UX prototypes, interactive feel, usability research and accessibility. Choosing which problems or mechanics to pursue and setting scope, system rules or balance is product management; producing standalone illustrations, sprites, audio, video or slide decks is media and asset production; implementing the working system is software engineering; prototype code alone is not software engineering.

title: Media and asset production
applies: Creating, rendering or editing visual, audio, video or presentation assets: illustrations, icons, sprites, diagrams, slide decks, audio tracks, voiceovers and video cuts. Designing product screen flows, UI controls and usability is design; writing persuasive customer copy is copywriting; prose documents, explanations and documentation are writing and editing; building the underlying application or game engine is software engineering; incidental charts, diagrams or conversion scripts inside another function's work do not count.

title: Software engineering
applies: Designing, writing, changing, debugging, testing, deploying or operating software, simulations and pipelines, including code review by engineers. Incidental scripts in service of another function do not count. Protection against abuse or compromise as an assigned objective is security; recurring business workflows are operations.

title: Security work
applies: Assessing and reducing unauthorized access, misuse, data exposure or compromise: security design, vulnerability analysis, security review and incident response. Ordinary implementation and reliability are software engineering; continuity of business workflows without a security objective is operations.

title: Data analysis
applies: Defining measures, preparing and analyzing quantitative datasets, estimating effects, building predictions, evaluating experiments and interpreting statistical evidence for decisions. Accounts and financial models are finance; empirical studies that advance scientific knowledge are scientific research; gathering qualitative sources or market facts is research work; using numbers inside another function does not count.

title: Research work
applies: Finding, verifying and synthesizing information from external, documentary or web sources: competitive intelligence, market or vendor surveys, literature and prior-art reviews, fact-checking and source dossiers. Empirical studies that test scientific hypotheses are scientific research; statistical analysis of a dataset is data analysis; audience research for positioning or campaigns is marketing; background lookups in service of another function do not count.

title: Scientific research
applies: Designing, conducting or synthesizing empirical studies to develop scientific knowledge: measurement, experiments, observational studies and computational investigations tied to empirical claims. Desk, web, vendor, market and general literature research are research work; substantial statistical work may also take data analysis.

title: Writing and editing
applies: Producing or substantively editing documents, explanations, articles, instructions and reference material, with responsibility for argument, organization, wording or editorial consistency. Routine messages do not count. Positioning, campaigns and channel choice are marketing; writing persuasive customer-facing copy is copywriting; producing standalone visual, audio, video or slide-deck assets is media and asset production; legal drafting is legal; gathering and verifying external sources as the main deliverable is research work; scientific interpretation is scientific research.

title: Quality review
applies: An assigned responsibility to test, playtest, review or assess others' deliverables for defects and fitness for use, such as QA or acceptance testing. A producer or integrator checking work it builds or assembles does not count. Review that needs a function's own expertise, such as legal review, code review by engineers, security assessment or peer review, is that function's work.
